questions.question: The non protein chemical compound required for enzyme activity derived from vitamins are (a) Coenzymes (b) Cofactors (c) Mg2+ (d) Heme
questions.solution_html:
• Holoenzymes represent the complete, catalytically active form of enzymes that
  • require non-protein components for function.
  • Complete enzyme complex consisting of apoenzyme (protein part) plus
  • cofactor (inorganic ion or organic coenzyme like NAD+), enabling full
  • catalytic activity.
  • Apoenzyme alone is inactive; cofactor binding induces proper conformation
  • and stabilizes transition states for substrate catalysis.
  • Examples include RNA polymerase holoenzyme (with sigma factor) for
  • transcription initiation and DNA polymerase III for replication.
  • Cofactors often derived from vitamins (e.g., FAD from riboflavin, CoA from
  • pantothenic acid) act as transient carriers of electrons, acyl groups, or
  • hydrides.
  • Essential in metabolic pathways; dissociation into apoenzyme yields inactive
  • form, providing regulatory control.

questions.question: Give a detailed account on holoenzyme.
questions.solution_html:
• Holoenzymes represent the complete, catalytically active form of enzymes that
  • require non-protein components for function.
  • Complete enzyme complex consisting of apoenzyme (protein part) plus
  • cofactor (inorganic ion or organic coenzyme like NAD+), enabling full
  • catalytic activity.
  • Apoenzyme alone is inactive; cofactor binding induces proper conformation
  • and stabilizes transition states for substrate catalysis.
  • Examples include RNA polymerase holoenzyme (with sigma factor) for
  • transcription initiation and DNA polymerase III for replication.
  • Cofactors often derived from vitamins (e.g., FAD from riboflavin, CoA from
  • pantothenic acid) act as transient carriers of electrons, acyl groups, or
  • hydrides.
  • Essential in metabolic pathways; dissociation into apoenzyme yields inactive
  • form, providing regulatory control. [.U,
